regions.summary: Apply the shared low-nibble correction to the high scratch byte, fold a high-nibble overflow into the low byte, and propagate its carry. X selects one of eight authored adjustment bytes; arithmetic remains byte-width.

units.name: CorrectResultPackedScratch
units.summary: Apply the shared low-nibble correction to the high scratch byte, fold a high-nibble overflow into the low byte, and propagate its carry. X selects one of eight authored adjustment bytes; arithmetic remains byte-width.

units.name: AddPackedResultAdjustment
units.summary: Add the X-indexed adjustment byte before the common low-nibble correction. This byte transform does not establish arbitrary decimal-input correctness.

units.name: CorrectResultLowNibble
units.summary: Preserve the high nibble, add six when the low nibble is at least ten, and combine with the high nibble under 6502 carry semantics.

units.name: FormatResultUnsignedByte
units.summary: Clear five output cells and format the unsigned byte as hundreds/tens/ones digit tiles offset by one. Leading zero suppression uses the existing result-buffer column convention.

units.name: FormatResultTensAndOnes
units.summary: Use repeated subtraction of ten to append tens and ones tiles, then clear the designated leading-zero cell.

units.name: RankSeriesScores
units.summary: Compare all 26 racer scores in the selected player plane to compute ranks, then collect up to ten display rows. If the player falls beyond ten, put the player in the final display row.

units.name: ReduceRacerSelectorBySixtyFour
units.summary: Subtract $40 up to twice with a balanced stack temporary. The authored racer/name representation determines the useful input domain.

units.name: SendResultAudioCommand
units.summary: Preserve command A while setting the saved PRG selection to four, then tail through the banked audio command entry.

units.name: TickResultAudio
units.summary: Set saved PRG selection four and service the banked audio update.

units.name: ResetResultAudio
units.summary: Send audio commands zero and one through the result bank-preserving command wrapper.

units.name: GetResultAudioControl
units.summary: Return the audio global control byte from CPU RAM $0600; no status or hardware register is read.

units.name: WaitShortResultInput
units.summary: Enable the frame source and set a 30-frame result input timeout.

units.name: EnableResultsFrameSource
units.summary: Enable NMI and the result PPU control mode in both the hardware register and shadow.

units.name: ClearPlayerCompletionAndResults
units.summary: Select the current player plane, clear its two completion counters and then clear 64 bytes of rank/result scratch.

units.name: ClearPlayerStandingScratch
units.summary: Clear 55 bytes of result scratch starting at the selected player offset. Caller must supply the established player plane base.

units.name: FormatPlacementSummary
units.summary: Emit the selected placement/count phrase when the saved placement is one through three; otherwise append a blank run. The later numeric clauses preserve the authored comparison behavior.

units.name: ComputePlayerResultOffsets
units.summary: A produces Y=A*2 and returns A*64 modulo 256, the two offsets used for completion and score planes.

units.name: ScaleResultPaletteSelector
units.summary: Continue the fixed shift chain used to select the 16-byte palette record.

units.name: SelectPlayerResultPlane
units.summary: Read the session player selector and compute its completion and 64-byte score-plane offsets, saving the latter in shared result scratch.

regions.summary: Entry requires one byte above a conventional return address, for example a caller push followed by JMP. Consume that argument; S=(argument+$6455) mod 256. If its low nibble is at least ten, T=(S+6) mod 256; otherwise T=S. Scratch $6456 retains T and A returns min(T,$60). This is not a general saturating decimal addition: $99+$65=$fe, then correction wraps to $04. No actual producer is recovered.

units.name: RunPitRepairAnimation

units.name: RunPitFuelAnimation
units.summary: Initialize 24 animation states and derive the fuel parameter from the active car setup, then run the second service animation.

units.name: RunBothPitServices
units.summary: Run the first 24-state service followed by the second, resetting each service's state/timing fields. Their precise authored repair/refuel presentation remains inferred from pit consumers.

units.name: FinishPitService
units.summary: Refresh final pit state, disable rendering, play the completion request and return through the pit exit setup.

units.name: AnimateFirstPitService
units.summary: Render two groups of components for each of 24 states. Between states update the clock/service meter, wait a setup-dependent number of frames and optionally reverse OAM ordering. A service status bit can hold the current state.

units.name: BuildFirstPitServiceFrame
units.summary: Reset the OAM allocator. Resolve two component-span selectors and translated origins from state-indexed arrays, draw both groups through the shared emitter and hide remaining OAM before advancing the animation state.

units.name: AnimateSecondPitService
units.summary: Clear the service-specific race bit and render multiple component groups for each of 24 states. The timed hold uses the opposite service-status polarity from the first animation.

units.name: BuildSecondPitServiceFrame
units.summary: Assemble the service scene from parallel Y/tile/attribute/X planes. Each group has state-selected start/end indices and translated origins; four repeated groups share geometry with alternate attributes/positions. Append through the common bounded OAM emitter.

units.name: HideUnusedServiceSprites
units.summary: Fill the remaining OAM bytes with $f8, advance the animation state and return after all 24 states; otherwise repeat the timed service frame.

units.name: EmitPitComponentSpan
units.summary: Inputs: four source pointers at $07/$09/$0b/$0d, Y=start, $bc=exclusive end, X=OAM offset and $0f/$10=Y/X origins. Emit translated four-byte sprites until the component end or OAM $f8. Commit the allocator and tail-call the sound wrapper, which restores caller PRG selection.
